topic.title: Equilibrium Learning in Sequential Multi-Agent Games
topic.overview: Multi-agent learning must account for other decision makers whose strategies affect both rewards and future states. This cluster studies equilibria in Markov and extensive-form games, including collaboration, competition, and imperfect information. Methods combine policy learning with optimization tools that exploit special game structure rather than assuming arbitrary games are easy to solve.
topic.whyItMatters: An individually improving agent can destabilize a learning system when opponents also adapt. Equilibrium guarantees clarify what collective behavior an algorithm targets and how much interaction or computation it may require under stated assumptions.
topic.evolution: Early representatives investigate friend-or-foe learning, beliefs, and graphical games. Later work develops actor–critic and policy-gradient guarantees for richer sequential settings. Recent sum-of-squares approaches address imperfect recall, offering convergence results and tractable special cases while retaining the broader computational difficulty.
openQuestions: Which structural assumptions remain realistic when agents learn from partial observations?
Can equilibrium guarantees coexist with scalable function approximation and limited interaction budgets?
